etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English dour (“severe”), originally from Early Scots dour (14th c.), of uncertain origin. Usually derived from Latin dūrus (“hard, stern”), but the vowel is problematic. One way of circumventing this problem is by assuming it was borrowed through (or influenced by) Scottish Gaelic dùr, from Middle Irish dúr, itself from the Latin. Doublet of dure.
The pronunciation with /ʊ/ is based on Scots and northernmost English dialects. That with /aʊ̯/ is the regular development in most of England, but may also be a spelling pronunciation.
